judges: WHAT IT IS: the per-run constraint heade
changes: C1 (bounds W1): Replace the open-ended PULL with a DIGEST contract — start/done boundaries read IDs + owners + review-by dates only (the JSON twins TASKBOX.json/DIRECTIVES.json the Stop hook already parses, plus an OPEN-LOOPS header digest), with an explicit ~2K-token cap; full OPEN-LOOPS body reads are scoped to rows this work touches. Rationale: research-coverage.md already proves the digest-not-dump pattern on this estate.

C2 (bounds W2): Ship with paths: frontmatter — and because the trigger is session-start it must be always-on, so per context-reduction.md §8 ('a new rule must replace bulk, not add') FOLD it into the existing AGENTS-RUNTIME §1c/§1d blocks as a 3-6 line boundary clause + pointer instead of a 28th standalone rule, or retire equivalent always-on bulk in the same change. Install authored-first, add the §12 row, then sync-rules + lint — and only AFTER DA-1's event-ordered back-propagation lands (a runtime-tree-first install is silently destroyed by the next sync).

C3 (bounds W3): Before relying on 'keep that lane intact', actually wire gap-check into the _dispatch Stop manifest (its 2.5s internal budget fits the 35s ceiling) and prove it fires — or rewrite the pairing clause to state plainly that the rule is context-only until the hook is wired. A rule claiming a mechanical backstop that is unwired on four probed surfaces is A-05's false-confidence class.

C4 (bounds W4): Replace 'always end with clean-or-a-write' with 'write ONLY rows for items this work touched and did not finish; every new row carries owner + review-by (gap-check's no-date check bites exactly there); expired rows are re-dated only with a one-line evidence note, never silently; rewrite-in-place, cap net row growth'. Add a weekly decay sweep so the register does not become the bloat it prevents.

C5 (bounds W6): Change 'the register wins' to 'the register wins POSITION pending one cheap disk/git probe; if the probe contradicts the register, the probe wins and the row is corrected in the same turn' — bringing the clause under single-signal-verification.md's instrument-wins rule instead of over it.

C6 (bounds W7): Bind start/done boundaries to the ORCHESTRATING session only; every subagent receives a <=10-line distilled position block, never raw register bytes; state explicitly that subagents do NOT read estate registers (resolves the inheritance contradiction and the DA-4 missing-rail degradation).

C7 (bounds W8): Add a de-minimis escape (trivial/single-file work: one-line TASKBOX check, no full boundary ceremony), and scope the workflows-registry pull to in-flight runs affecting the current task until L-57's reconciliation closes (the registry self-reports 8 duplicate meta_names today).

C8 (meter the mandate): One week after ship, measure and record: boundary tokens added (median/p90), new OPEN-LOOPS rows per week, gap-check injection frequency before/after, SessionStart duration delta. The owner's 'no disbenefits of any form' mandate is only checkable with numbers; if gap-check noise rises or median boundary cost exceeds ~3K tokens, tighten C1. UNVERIFIED until measured.

DISBENEFIT GATE (regression lens) — VERDICT: SHIP-WITH-CHANGES. KILL if the changes are refused (rationale at end). All citations read this run, 2026-09-30.

WHAT THE DRAFT IS TODAY: prompt-stage only. `task-list-above-session-context.md` exists in NEITHER rules tree (Read: File does not exist; Grep across C:\Users\Prekzursil\.agents finds the string only in knowledge\council-runs\2026-09-30-discipline-rules\full-result.json). Both trees hold 27 rules each (Glob), so shipping means becoming the 28th.

THE WORST REALISTIC CASE, lane by lane:

W1 — UNBOUNDED PER-BOUNDARY TOKEN TAX (latency + context). The rule mandates PULL of TASKBOX + OPEN-LOOPS + DIRECTIVES + workflows registry "before the first substantive action, and after every compaction/resume", plus re-read at every done boundary, with NO cap and NO digest requirement. Measured sizes (Read this run): OPEN-LOOPS.md 256 dense lines (~44KB, ~11K tokens, approximate bytes/4), DIRECTIVES.md 127 lines (~5K), TASKBOX.md 35 lines (~1.2K), workflows-registry.md 133+ lines (~2.5K). Literal compliance = ~20K tokens + 4-6 tool calls per boundary; even careful compliance = 3-5K. On THIS box that is not abstract: chronic RAM pressure ("simple PowerShell commands can take minutes", HOME AGENTS.md Learned Workspace Facts) and measured SessionStart starvation p50 4242ms / max 13841ms / 40 timeouts (OPEN-LOOPS.md:240, L-42). Post-compaction is the worst moment: re-injecting ~20K tokens into a freshly compacted window accelerates the NEXT auto-compact — the exact bloat context-reduction.md §8 bars ("A new rule must replace bulk, not add"; measured standing violation ~14.7k always-on tokens, OPEN-LOOPS.md:105, A-10). Almost certain (92%) some sessions do full reads, because the draft gives no digest clause and literal compliance is the observed norm.

W2 — INERT-ON-ARRIVAL + NET CONTEXT ADD. The draft has NO `paths:` frontmatter. A-05 (OPEN-LOOPS.md:97) is the measured precedent: four rules deployed 2026-09-25 were deployed-but-INERT for exactly this reason — "deployment is placement, not loadability". Shipped verbatim, the rule loads nowhere while everyone believes it binds (A-05's own verdict: a gate that passes on the broken state manufactures false confidence). To bind at session start it must be always-on — becoming the 4th always-on rule in a set A-05 records as deliberately tiny ("always-on rules are context cost every session"), adding ~350-400 tokens to every session with zero bulk removed. Install-order hazard: DA-1 (OPEN-LOOPS.md:219) — runtime-tree-only rule edits are silently destroyed by the next sync-rules.ps1, and its deadline is EVENT-ORDERED (before ANY sync).

W3 — THE ENFORCEMENT PAIRING IS BUILT ON A DEAD LANE. The draft's escape hatch is "this rule is context, not enforcement — the gap-check Stop hook reads the registers mechanically; keep that lane intact." Four independent wiring surfaces probed this run, all NEGATIVE for gap-check: (1) settings.json Stop hooks = dispatcher.py(5s) + _dispatch/dispatch.py(35s) + profile-capture only (settings.json:597-629); (2) hooks/_dispatch/manifest.json Stop = 7 checks, no gap-check (manifest.json:96-167); (3) grep of .agents\harness = zero gap-check references; (4) grep of .claude\hooks = zero references. gap_check.py itself is healthy code (Read, 306 lines, BUDGET_S=2.5 at :47, REGISTER at :48) — but it is GREEN-not-LIVE, the identical defect class the manifest documents twice about its own checks (manifest.json:164 dark-surface comment; :224 edit-validate "GREEN-not-LIVE defect"). UNVERIFIED residual: a fifth wiring surface I did not read; confidence gap-check is unwired: almost certain (90%). Consequence: as drafted, the rule is pure voluntary context with a phantom backstop — the AGENTS-RUNTIME §1c enforcement table's gap-check row is currently aspirational.

W4 — WRITE-PRESSURE → GAP-CHECK NOISE LOOP (when gap-check IS wired). "ALWAYS end a boundary check with either 'registers clean for this scope' or a register write — silence is not a check" invites reflexive row-writes. gap_check.py flags exactly the artifacts sloppy rows produce: no-review-by rows, CLOSED-with-empty-evidence, expired review-by (gap_check.py:162-170). The register sits ~72h from an expiry cliff: ~13 rows carry review-by 2026-09-30..10-02 (L-34, DA-1, DA-2 at :219-220 due TODAY; L-06/L-10/L-22/L-24/A-01/A-09/A-13/A-14/A-15 at 10-01/02). The done-boundary NEVER ("never declare done while a register shows an in-scope open item you created or touched") collides with a register whose rows are mostly owner-gated (Owner=O): the only compliant exits are fixing owner-only items (impossible) or re-registering them — date-inflation churn that erodes the expiry semantics gap-check depends on. Either the Stop hook fires forever (noise, violating its own docstring contract "no downsides while also not being noise") or it gets tuned out (worse). Concurrency: OPEN-LOOPS.md is one hand-edited file with a recorded stash-pop UU collision from concurrent lane edits (OPEN-LOOPS.md:11, :186-193) — more writers at more boundaries = more lost rows. Likely (70%).

W5 — ALWAYS-PUSH / AUTOPUSH INTERACTION (real but low severity). Register writes live in ~/.agents, a git repo per two independent documentary signals (gap_check.py:49 REPO + git ops; OPEN-LOOPS.md:186-193 "git pull --rebase in C:\Users\Prekzursil\.agents", commit 4668b0413 owning register rows) though the env header reports "Is a git repository: false" — UNVERIFIED which detector is right. post-commit-autopush exists (scripts/git-hooks/post-commit-autopush; DIRECTIVES.md:21-28, D-1, installed in 3 repos). Worst chain: every done-boundary register write → commit (harness-vcs-hygiene: live-authored harness files must reconcile to the repo before "done") → autopush → stream of tiny pushes; every UNCOMMITTED register write → git-hygiene SessionStart drift injection (manifest.json:83-93, 30s budget on the already-starved SessionStart lane of L-42); any push failure → gap-check's unpushed-count alarm (gap_check.py:240-269) exercised by register churn until the "autopush broke" signal is noise. Likely (75%), low severity, compounding on three already-loaded lanes.

W6 — PRECEDENCE INVERSION OVER LIVE INSTRUMENTS. "When in-session recollection and a register disagree on position, the register wins... Rebuild the plan from the register." The evidence carve-out does not cover load-bearing POSITION claims, and this register has documented refuted positions: L-21's "distro is NOT unbootable — refuted by fresh probe" (OPEN-LOOPS.md:22, the register previously said the opposite), L-30 recording UNVERIFIED lane claims written into the register (:214), D-06 owner correction over a baked-in lens verdict (:78). This collides with the ALWAYS-ON rule single-signal-verification.md: "When a claim and an instrument you are already running disagree, the instrument wins" — a higher-precedence deployed rule. Worst case: a post-compaction session rebuilds from a stale row and re-does shipped work — the exact re-run failure research-coverage.md exists to prevent. Likely (60-70%) at least once in the first month if unchanged; severity medium-high.

W7 — FAN-OUT COST MULTIPLIER + SUBAGENT CONTRADICTION. "ALWAYS hand register-derived position to every spawned subagent explicitly", with no digest cap. context-reduction.md §7: each subagent is a COLD cache — everything in the prompt is fixed context. A 200-500-token position block x the estate's signature 50-100-agent fan-outs = 20-50K tokens per run of position boilerplate. The done boundary is not scoped orchestrator-only, so a literal subagent reading demands re-reading registers subagents were just told they do not inherit — contradiction, or 4N extra reads. DA-4 (OPEN-LOOPS.md:222) proves the failure shape: lens spawns already start WITHOUT file rails and degrade to NOT-CHECKED — a clause assuming every spawn can read registers silently no-ops in exactly the fan-outs it targets.

W8 — OWNER FRICTION. The start pull surfaces 60+ rows, many deliberately owner-parked (L-50/L-51/L-52 are explicit owner calls). Combined with §1c ask-in-tiers, worst case: every session opens by re-triaging parked decisions before a one-line typo fix — no de-minimis escape exists ("before the first substantive action" catches everything), contra owner-ops §0/§6 (no permission theater, execute > lecture) and §1's EVPI gate. The workflows-registry pull imports known-inconsistent state: the registry self-reports 8 duplicate meta_names to reconcile and 515 session-embedded names (workflows-registry.md:40-51), mid-reconciliation under OPEN loop L-57 (:255). Almost certain (90%) it contains stale entries today.

HONEST COUNTERWEIGHTS (why not KILL outright): the target defect is real and measured (orphaned deferrals, compaction dropping OPEN-LOOPS — the compact-instructions block exists because of it; DA-4 lanes degrading to NOT-CHECKED); the done boundary mostly MECHANIZES already-binding §1c doctrine; the rule's own text is ~400 tokens; every cost above lives in the UNSPECIFIED execution shape (full-read vs digest, per-spawn vs distilled, unconditional vs scoped, backstop assumed vs verified).

KILL CONDITION: if the council will not take the changes below, KILL — on this specific box (starved SessionStart, ~44KB register, ~13 rows expiring in 72h, four-surface-unwired gap-check), the draft as written is a net-disbenefit machine: unbounded pulls, phantom enforcement, register-over-instrument steering, and write-pressure that converts the one hook whose design contract is "silent when clean" into permanent noise.
